> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5f87b30caf58d0108de30ba747ee18f085a5972a` — the merge of head `23bebd666bc6cc6617321a5a3090847f0760bdb9` into base `3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5f87b30caf58d0108de30ba747ee18f085a5972a && git checkout 5f87b30caf58d0108de30ba747ee18f085a5972a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575 23bebd666bc6cc6617321a5a3090847f0760bdb9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575 && git merge --no-ff 23bebd666bc6cc6617321a5a3090847f0760bdb9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b46855fb97365902e1e81a6484cd41bd363e575` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `23bebd666bc6cc6617321a5a3090847f0760bdb9`
Local-runs: none

Family F3 of ruling 6182001882 (items 3 and 7) on card #23543, PR #23742, read at 2026-10-16T00:24Z. Inputs: the card body and its seventeen comments, the PR body and its 16-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge-base `3b46855fb9` (+621/−129, equal to the three-dot diff against `origin/main` `140238a47b`), the precedent diffs of PR #23600 (F1) and PR #23638 (F5-jsx) with their contract reviews, and the 41 check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; every tree reading below is `git show` / `git grep` against the fetched head. objectui was not read: the ruling names no objectui half for F3.

**Gate verdicts on this head:** 41 check-runs, 36 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 0 failing or pending. The five required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and 1–6/6), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — are all `success`; so are `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`, the four `Type Check ·` lanes, the nine `Lint ·` lanes, and the card, claim, single-writer and Part-of guards. The 5 `skipped` are the PR fast-set skips (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the opt-in packed-tarball smoke), measured by `main`'s full battery, not on the PR.

Governance: none of the 16 paths is in `GOVERNED_SURFACES` (register read on the head); head repo equals base repo; draft; `Part of #23543` is the first line and no closing keyword follows; the assignee mirrors the card's; 750 changed lines; no `content/docs/releases/` edit.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes (each narrows what an author may write):

1. **The flow parse refuses every named loose key under a `wait` or `connector_action` node's `config`** (`flow.zod.ts` superRefine, in the `collectFlowGraphs` walk beside `connectorActionConfigRefusals`, so a region-body node is reached; `siblingBlockLooseConfigRefusals` in the new leaf `automation/flow-sibling-block-loose-keys.ts`). One `custom` issue per key at `nodes.N.config.KEY`: "A `wait` node's `config.duration` was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0087 D2) … Move it to `waitEventConfig.timerDuration` …", then the house `os migrate meta --from 16` sentence (both lifts are step-17 members, `migrations/registry.ts.template:1099-1100`). Refused: `eventType`, `timerDuration`, `duration`, `signalName`, `signal`, `timeoutMs` on `wait`; `connectorId`, `actionId`, `input` on `connector_action`; a key present with `null` too (only `=== undefined` is skipped, and JSON cannot carry it). Not refused: any other `config` key on these types (`note`), and the same keys on another node type — both pinned as controls. At `defineStack` it is `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 with the one issue at `flows.0.nodes.1.config.KEY` when the block is complete. **RIGHT** — ruling item 3's "refused with the prescription naming the sibling block", at every door of the authoring funnel: `normalizeStackInput` replays live entries only (`apply.ts:156`; no `includeRetired` anywhere under `stack*.ts` or the CLI's validate and compile paths), so `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`, and `os lint` through a config that calls `defineStack`. `tsc` cannot carry it (`FlowNodeSchema.config` is an open record), so the parse-time prescription is the whole channel, as item 7 says; the runtime strings cite the ADR and no tracker number.

2. **One table, two readers.** `WAIT_EVENT_CONFIG_LOOSE_KEYS` / `CONNECTOR_CONFIG_LOOSE_KEYS` moved byte for byte from `registry.ts` into the leaf; `registry.ts` imports them (`:49`) and the refusal reads them, so the refused set and the lifted set cannot drift (pinned: `refuses every named loose key and no other`). The leaf is not on the automation barrel, the spec `exports` map carries fixed subpaths only (no `./automation/*` wildcard) and `files` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` only, so no public module appears; `check:generated` reads 14 artifacts up to date on the head (api-surface and export-origins unchanged). **RIGHT.**

3. **Both lifts leave the load path** (`retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, the value `conversions/types.ts` gives for an `18.0.0-next.N` label; the package reads `18.0.0-next.1`). The funnel no longer rewrites an authored loose key (pinned: stack unchanged, zero notices); the data-at-rest seams replay them under `includeRetired`: the engine's `registerFlow` canonicalizer (`engine.ts:4576`), `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (`stored.ts:107`, pinned true), the artifact-ingestion door inside its window, and the metadata save door's flow path (judgment 6). Neither `CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION` (`engine.ts:2251`) nor `FLOW_FALLBACK_VERDICT_NOT_REPLAYED` (`protocol.ts:3240`) names either entry — each list holds only the decision-mode default flip. **RIGHT** — item 3's "both entries set `retiredFromLoadPath`".

4. **The lifts now DELETE a loose key that does not lift, with a notice** (`liftWaitEventConfig`, `liftConnectorConfigShape`). Three cases, each read against the `??` chain the lifts mirror: (a) a key the block shadows — never read, the declared value won; (b) a later candidate shadowed by the first present one (`duration` beside `timerDuration`) — never read, the chain stopped at the first present value; (c) a `null` — the chain skipped it and the old lift left it in place; it is still skipped for precedence (the next candidate lifts: pinned) and now deleted. Precedence is unchanged in every case; what changes is that the stored row comes back with the block alone, which it must, because judgment 1 now refuses the kept key at the parse the seam runs next (`FlowSchema.parse(converted)`). The connector completeness guard is unchanged: a node whose pair cannot complete returns untouched and is refused at the block and at each loose key (pinned: `nodes.1.connectorConfig`, `nodes.1.config.connectorId`) — it never loaded. **RIGHT** — item 3's "the lift deletes a loose key the block shadows at rehydration, so stored flows keep loading"; (b) and (c) are the same deletion for the same reason (a value no reading ever reached) and sit inside the letter, not beyond it: without them a stored `{ timerDuration, duration }` or `{ timerDuration: null, … }` row would stop loading at 18, the exact hazard the ruling closes. Pinned end to end: `registerFlow` on a block-plus-shadowed-`input` row registers, `config` comes back `{}`, and the action receives the block's input (`connector-nodes.test.ts`); the wait case asserts the deleted loose key the same way (`wait-node.test.ts`).

5. **`config.timeoutMs` is prescribed as `waitEventConfig.timerDuration`, as a string.** The block spelling `waitEventConfig.timeoutMs` is itself a 17 tombstone, and the chain's end state for a stored `config.timeoutMs: 60000` is `timerDuration: '60000'`: the wait lift moves it onto `waitEventConfig.timeoutMs`, then `flow-node-wait-timeout-keys-removed`, ordered after it in the chain (`registry.ts:16730`, `:16751`), stringifies it onto `timerDuration` when that is unset and drops it otherwise (`removeWaitTimeoutKeys`, whose docblock records "`timeoutMs` moves to `timerDuration` rather than being dropped, because that IS what it did"). The prescription states that end state and its "already set — delete" branch. **RIGHT** — a prescription naming `waitEventConfig.timeoutMs` would send the author into a second tombstone.

6. **The metadata save door, read off the code path, not the changeset's words.** A NEW authored save of a flow carrying a named loose key through the metadata API (`POST /meta`, Studio draft or publish) is **not refused; it is lifted and accepted**. With an automation service reachable, `resolveFlowCanonicalizer()` is the engine's `canonicalizeFlow` (`protocol.ts:22685-22775`, `engine.ts:4576`): `applyConversionsToFlow(…, { includeRetired: true, excludeConversionIds: CONVERSIONS_NOT_REPLAYED_AT_REHYDRATION })`, then `FlowSchema.parse(converted)`; the body persisted is `result.storable`, the lifted shape with the shadowed key deleted, one notice per key on the engine logger and nothing to the caller. Without one, the fallback judges `flowGateVerdictBody = applyConversionsToFlow(request.item, { includeRetired: true, … })` (`:22771`) and persists the RAW body, loose key kept, for `registerFlow` to lift on the next boot — the `[#21982]` posture ("the FULL chain, retired entries included — #23487 retired those spellings from the authoring funnel, not from this seam"). So the changeset's "still replays both conversions" is exact, and the D3 entry says it in plain words ("a script that still sends the loose spelling keeps saving").
   - **Is that a second accepted spelling at a door that judges authored input?** At that one door, for an API caller, it is: the F5-jsx record's "after this PR no door accepts the spelling from an author or an API caller" does not hold for F3, because the page door parses `request.item` raw and refuses while the flow door converts first and accepts. **Is it this PR's double spelling?** No. The door is untouched by this diff (`protocol.ts` is outside the claim's surface and unchanged); its posture predates the ruling as a recorded verdict (#4542, #21982, and the contract-tier review 6177406940 that passed the seven #23487 retirements through this same door); and it is the flow door's posture for every retired flow entry, not for these two. `conversions/types.ts:246-272` draws `retiredFromLoadPath`'s jurisdiction at the authoring funnel and names flow rehydration in the automation engine a data-at-rest seam, and the flow save door IS that canonicalizer (`canonicalizeStoredFlow`, named for the row it writes); the ruling's item 3 was decided on the presentation's premise that "the rehydration seam parses the same schema". Reversing that posture is a decision on `protocol.ts` for every retired flow entry (Prime Directive #13), not an F3 rider, and the dev was right not to take it inside this claim. **RIGHT as a disclosed inheritance; the boundary is escalated in ③ item 9**, because F2's flow half (`retryDelayMs` → `backoffMs`) and F5-http (`http_request` → `http`) meet the same door, and one answer should serve all three families.

7. **Readers and fixtures.** Both executors already read only their blocks (`wait-node.ts:225`, `connector-nodes.ts:55`); the connector descriptor publishes no `configSchema` (`connector-nodes.ts:39`, deliberate since #4045), so a schema-driven form cannot be re-taught the loose shape; only comments moved, and they now say what judgment 1 and 3 say. Head-tree sweep for a named loose key under `config` outside tests, across `packages/**`, `examples/**`, `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` and the service-automation README: zero writers (the showcase, the skills example `examples-flows.md` and `connectors.mdx` author the blocks; the only hits are release-owned CHANGELOG quotations, which stay). The five re-spelled fixtures (two lint suites, `run-summary.test.ts`) used the retired location without testing the lift; `connector-action-config-required.test.ts` now pins the three-issue shape. **RIGHT.**

8. **Verdict-list pin and D3 entry.** `conversions.test.ts`: both entries move from the kept list — now exactly the four entries of F2, F4 and F5-http (`flow-node-http-callout-rename`, `page-component-visibility-to-visibleWhen`, `retry-policy-converged`, `view-visibleOn-to-visibleWhen`) — to the retired list with `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`; the new describe pins the three claims that must hold together (a stored loose-only row and a block-plus-shadowed row each refused as written and loading after the seam's replay with the block alone; the funnel no longer rewrites; `defineStack` refuses naming the block key). `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` gains one refusal row per entry in its `JOIN`, so every retired entry still has a renderer. `18.flow-sibling-block-loose-config-keys-refused.ts` is a `SemanticMigration` in the sibling shape, `conversionIds` naming both entries; both registry fixtures show the deleted shadowed key and `expectedNotices` goes 4 → 5. **RIGHT** — item 7's "verdict-list pin updated", shrinking the kept-without-ruling list by exactly two.

9. **Docs.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`: the `connectorConfig` and `waitEventConfig` rows name the refusal. No `.describe()` moved, so `content/docs/references/` is untouched, rightly. **RIGHT.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23543-f3-retire-wait-connector-config-lift.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/service-automation: patch`; summary `feat(spec)!:`; `**BREAKING (authoring):**` banner; FROM → TO for every refused key, the `timeoutMs` special case, the "block already set — delete" rule, the `os migrate meta --from 16` sentence, how stored rows keep loading, and the ADR-0087 disposition marker `registered flow-sibling-block-loose-config-keys-refused`, which names the D3 entry's id exactly. **RIGHT.** The repo is in Changesets pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), where a BREAKING spec change grades `minor`; the F1 and F5-jsx changesets carry the identical frontmatter, banner and arm shape. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries `check-adr-0087-registration`) are `success`.
- **Rows.** `spec` is the one package whose published behaviour changes. `service-automation`'s two source edits are comment-only; F1's record took no row for comment-only moves (`cli`, `service-datasource`), and the dev's `patch` row here (flagged in its report) is the other defensible reading — the shipped source text changed — at the cost of one no-op patch in pre mode. Accepted, not owed. `lint` moved only test files and `metadata-protocol` is untouched: no row is owed and none is missing.
- **The `Clause-②:` line.** The changeset's `yes (narrowing)` is the ruling's spelling (item 7) and the right arm: judgments 1–4 narrow; the widening `yes` names is the published upgrade catalogue (the D3 entry ships in the spec tarball's `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` / `spec-changes.json`), as the F5-jsx record counted it — with no new export this time. The PR body's line 2 reads bare `Clause-②: yes`: the gap F1's record ③ item 1 named, from the same source — the claim 6203354520 wrote the bare line and the dev copied it. No gate reads the arm from the body (`check-changeset-no-major` reads `yes` and finds `spec` at `minor`; the registration gate takes the arm from the changeset), so it is not a condition of this record; the body is the PR-scoped carrier, and the owning seat amends it to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` before the PR is armed, the body read back after the write. See ③ item 1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (6204710307):

1. *A `connector_action` node with only `config.connectorId` / `config.actionId` gets three issues (the missing block plus one per loose key): keep, or suppress the per-key issues when the block is absent?* **The seat answers A, and A is right.** The accept set is identical either way — the node is refused in both — so this is presentation inside the ruling, not a decision for the card: each issue is true and located where the author wrote the key, the block issue already names the move, and B would add a special case to a rule that is otherwise one table, the drift the leaf exists to prevent. Pinned on the head (`connector-action-config-required.test.ts`; the completeness-guard case in `conversions.test.ts`). Riding this item, the seat's one-line edit: the body's `Clause-②` arm (②).

Dev `deviations`:

2. *File surface widened by the pin sweep.* **Accepted** — each is a fixture or a doc row named in the report and re-read in ① judgment 7; `registry.ts`'s hunks are the import and the two entries only (13 hunks, between lines 46 and 1788), `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` and every other entry untouched, as the claim required.
3. *Executors comment-only; `service-automation` still at `patch`.* **Accepted** (②).
4. *The `os migrate meta` load-path suites unchanged; F2 inherits the no-live-subject question.* **Verified on the head:** `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-load-conversions.test.ts`, `migrate-meta-composed-load-conversions.test.ts`, `migrate-meta-composed.test.ts` and `spec/src/stack-authored-input.test.ts` all drive `retry-policy-converged` (8 / 9 / 5 / 1 references) and none names an F3 key. **Escalated to the F2 dispatch order on #23543**, as the F1 record's item 9 already carried it: F2 is the family that retires their last live subject, so its PR gives the authored-input shim a synthetic probe or retires the suites.
